text: EX-99.1 2 a20261030pressrelease.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 LCI Board Determines that the Unsolicited, Non-Binding Proposal from Monomoy Capital Partners Does Not Constitute a Superior Proposal LCI Industries Reiterates Support for Merger with Patrick ELKHART, Ind. – LCI Industries (NYSE: LCII) (“LCI”), today announced that its Board of Directors, in consultation with its outside financial and legal advisors, has unanimously determined that the unsolicited, non-binding proposal received from Monomoy Capital Partners to acquire LCI for $101 per share in cash does not constitute a superior proposal and is not reasonably likely to lead to a superior proposal. In reviewing Monomoy’s proposal, the Board of Directors carefully considered several factors and determined that a merger with Patrick Industries (NASDAQ: PATK) (“Patrick”) remains the best path towards long-term sustainable value creation for shareholders. Through its review, the LCI Board of Directors determined that Monomoy's proposal substantially undervalues LCI: • On a standalone basis: Monomoy's proposal fails to reflect the fundamental value of LCI's standalone business. As part of the LCI Board of Directors’ review, LCI, with the assistance of its advisors, updated its long-range plan, including to reflect the prevailing headwinds in the RV industry. Based on that updated plan, the valuation analysis of LCI on a standalone basis implies a midpoint discounted cash flow value in excess of $150 per share—materially above Monomoy’s proposal of $101 per share. • When evaluating Monomoy’s proposal against the value creation opportunity of the combination with Patrick: Compared to the compelling financial benefits of the combination with Patrick, Monomoy’s proposal is materially below the implied value of LCI’s shareholders pro forma ownership in the combined company, including the meaningful incremental value creation opportunity resulting from approximately $150 million of net run-rate cost synergies expected to be achieved within three years of closing and participation in the future growth prospects of a fundamentally stronger company with the firepower and flexibility to support continued investment in growth and capital returns. LCI and Patrick are making continued progress toward closing and remain on track to complete the transaction in the first half of 2027, subject to approval by shareholders of both companies, the receipt of required regulatory approvals, and the satisfaction of other customary closing conditions. In connection with the proposed transaction between LCI and Patrick, LCI and Patrick have both filed a supplement to their joint proxy statement/prospectus that contains updated information with the SEC which can be found on their respective investor relations websites. The LCI Board of Directors continues to recommend in favor of the Patrick transaction and encourages shareholders to vote their shares “FOR” the merger with Patrick at the Special Meeting scheduled for November 18, 2026. Perella Weinberg Partners LP is serving as financial advisor and Kirkland & Ellis LLP is serving as legal advisor to LCI Industries. About LCI Industries LCI Industries (NYSE: LCII), through its Lippert subsidiary, is a global leader in supplying engineered components to the outdoor recreation and transportation markets. We believe our innovative culture, advanced manufacturing capabilities, and dedication to enhancing the customer experience have established Lippert as a reliable partner for both OEM and aftermarket customers. For more information, visit www.lippert.com. Important Information About the Proposed Transaction and Where to Find It In connection with the proposed transaction between the Company and Patrick, Patrick has filed relevant materials with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”), including, among other filings, a Patrick registration statement on Form S-4 (File No. 333-299100) that includes a preliminary joint proxy statement of the Company and Patrick that also constitutes a prospectus of Patrick with respect to shares of Patrick’s common stock to be issued in the proposed transaction. The registration statement was declared effective by the SEC on October 19, 2026, and the Company and Patrick commenced mailing the definitive joint proxy statement/prospectus (the “Joint Proxy Statement/Prospectus”) to their respective stockholders on or about October 19, 2026. The Company and Patrick may also file other documents with the SEC regarding the proposed transaction.
